documents.abstract: Large language model (LLM) computer-use agents are typically evaluated with clean written instructions, despite speech being an increasingly popular interface for interacting with such systems. Speech input introduces an additional failure point: transcription errors can alter task-critical entities, constraints, or targets before the agent begins reasoning, while conventional ASR metrics do not directly measure whether the information required for successful execution has been preserved. We introduce Talk2Agent, a benchmark for evaluating how effectively voice interfaces convey human-spoken instructions to LLM-based computer-use agents. Talk2Agent builds human-spoken versions of tasks from WildClawBench and OSWorld and evaluates a range of voice interfaces, including dedicated ASR models, audio-capable LLMs, contextual biasing, and LLM-based ontology repair. Because repeatedly executing long-horizon computer-use tasks is costly and stochastic, we further propose an execution-free, task-conditioned evaluation framework that projects the original task grader onto prompt-addressable intentions and measures how much task-relevant information is retained after the voice interface. On WildClawBench, Talk2Agent's execution-free native projection provides a practical, execution-grounded measure of voice-interface quality, correlating with downstream task completion and improving Pearson correlation by 0.246 over WER/CER on 32 hours of real human speech.

Large language model-powered mobile agents can compose messages, manage files, operate financial applications, and act on content from other applications. Binary allow-or-refuse safeguards fit this setting poorly: some requests are safe to execute, some require confirmation, and some should be blocked. TapGuard is a task-level pre-execution router combining a compact semantic encoder, temperature-scaled three-class probabilities, a fixed rule floor, and confidence-triggered confirmation. Experiments used 150 canonical MobileSafetyBench release 3 tasks and 100 paired action-hint variants under instruction-template and task-category holdout protocols. Under template holdout, TapGuard lowered severity-weighted direct-execution exposure from 35.7% for the MiniLM semantic classifier to 27.7%, while low-risk direct execution declined from 64.0% to 54.0%. The frozen-cue router achieved still lower exposure but directly executed only 18.0% of low-risk tasks. TapGuard increased severe-risk blocking relative to MiniLM without achieving the highest three-way macro-F1. Category holdout showed the same broad trade-off. Privacy, offensiveness, and image-linked cases remained difficult, and generalization to unseen injection patterns was not established. These findings support evaluating mobile safety routing through both protection and preserved automation.

Multi-UAV multi-sensor cooperative detection is critical for situational awareness in complex environments with stationary known targets. To overcome the shortcomings of existing task allocation models in fine-grained cooperation, stealth constraints, and large-scale optimization, this paper proposes a new offline mission pre-planning method for static target scenarios. A five-layer hierarchical resource scheduling model is established, covering task, UAV platform, sensor type, cooperative mode, and execution role. Stealth requirements are incorporated as hard constraints, and a bi-objective optimization model is formulated to maximize weighted detection efficacy. A statistical adaptive genetic algorithm (SAGA) is developed as an offline pre-planning algorithm, featuring a coupled chromosome encoding strategy that integrates the five decision layers and an adaptive crossover-mutation mechanism guided by the Wilcoxon signed-rank test with effect size monitoring. Simulation results across small, medium, and large scenarios show that the SAGA achieves the highest mean best fitness in all scenarios. Compared with the GA, the improvement is statistically significant in the large-scale scenario, while in small- and medium-scale scenarios the differences from the GA and AGA are not significant. Compared with an improved whale optimization algorithm, the SAGA achieves statistically significantly higher best fitness and shorter computational time in all scenarios and converges significantly faster in small- and medium-scale scenarios. However, the SAGA requires longer computation time than the GA and AGA due to the per-generation statistical test. All allocations strictly satisfy the prescribed stealth constraints in the simulation model. The proposed method provides a novel, quantitatively validated solution for fine-grained, constraint-aware, and computationally efficient multi-UAV multi-sensor cooperative detection mission pre-planning.

AIM: To examine how task source and disease severity influence cognitive workload and decision-making performance among intensive care unit nurses during concurrent multitasking. Understanding how different clinical information sources influence nurses' decision-making may provide insights for supporting decision-making in complex critical care environments. DESIGN: A laboratory-based 2 × 2 mixed-design experimental study. METHODS: Thirty ICU nurses participated in a concurrent task prioritization task in which task source (machine-induced vs. human-induced) and disease severity (high vs. low) were manipulated. Eye-tracking measures, including fixation, saccade, blink, and pupil diameter metrics, together with decision accuracy, were collected during 80 task trials per participant. RESULTS: Decision accuracy was significantly higher for machine-induced tasks than for human-induced tasks and was also higher under high-severity conditions than under low-severity conditions. Significant main effects of task source were observed across multiple eye-tracking measures. Compared with human-induced tasks, machine-induced tasks were associated with higher cognitive workload, reflected by increased total fixation duration, fixation count, saccade count, and pupil diameter. Disease severity significantly affected several eye-tracking measures; however, these effects were mainly observed during human-induced tasks, with no significant severity-related differences during machine-induced tasks. CONCLUSION: Task source and disease severity influence cognitive processing patterns during ICU multitasking. Higher cognitive workload does not necessarily impair clinical decision accuracy, and task-related information characteristics play a critical role in shaping decision-making performance. IMPLICATIONS FOR THE PROFESSION: The findings highlight the need for nursing practice to consider how different sources of task demands shape cognitive processing during multitasking. Recognizing that higher cognitive workload may support accurate decision-making under certain information conditions can inform task prioritization, clinical training, and the cognition-sensitive decision support for ICU nurses. IMPACT: This work advances evidence-based understanding of cognitive workload and decision-making in intensive care nursing. PATIENT OR PUBLIC CONTRIBUTION: No patient or public contribution.

The rapid proliferation of artificial intelligence (AI) in educational systems has fundamentally altered how knowledge is delivered, assessed, and personalized, raising profound questions about the spiritual and psychological dimensions of learning that algorithmic systems are structurally ill-equipped to address. This library research study investigates the role of Islamic counseling grounded in the Qur’anic principle of tawazun (balance) as a necessary and substantive counterbalance to the mechanistic logic of AI-driven education. Using a systematic content analysis of peer-reviewed literature, Islamic pedagogical texts, and international policy documents on educational technology, this study argues that tawazun offers not merely a cultural supplement but an epistemological corrective to the efficiency-first paradigm underlying most AI educational tools. The findings reveal three critical imbalances produced by AI-driven education: the suppression of intrinsic motivation through algorithmic reward structures, the erosion of relational pedagogy, and the neglect of students’ spiritual formation. Islamic counseling, through its integration of muhasabah (self-reflection), tawakkul (reliance on God), and ukhuwah (solidarity), is demonstrated to restore these dimensions in ways no AI system can replicate. This paper contributes a theoretically grounded model the Tawazun Counseling Framework (TCF) for integrating Islamic guidance within AI-augmented educational environments, with implications for curriculum designers, school counselors, and policymakers in Muslim-majority educational institutions.

As the adoption of flipped classroom methods (FCM) continues to grow in higher education, understanding the factors that promote students' learning engagement is crucial. While teachers' autonomy support (TAS) is widely recognized to enhance it, the underlying mechanism remains largely unexplored within the context. Based on Self-Determination Theory (SDT) and Constructivist Learning Theory, the study examined the mediating effects of students' intrinsic motivation (IM) and self-regulated learning (SRL) between TAS and learning engagement in a cross-sectional research design. Data were collected from 360 university students across six Indian states, and mediation analysis was incorporated. The findings disclosed that TAS positively impacts the learning engagement of the students directly and indirectly by fostering IM and SRL. It supports the propositions of the two theories. It suggests that autonomy-supportive pedagogical practices fashion psychologically empowering learning environments that, in turn, encourage learners to actively participate, thus creating effective student-centered flipped classroom environments. Educators should bring about conducive environments for effective pedagogy employment by offering choices, explaining rationales behind given tasks, and acknowledging student perspectives to nurture their motivation and self-regulated learning.

Generative artificial intelligence is reshaping teaching, learning, assessment, and professional practice in English as a Foreign Language. However, little is known about how university teachers exercise professional reasoning within emerging AI governance environments. This embedded qualitative multiple-case study explored how university teachers of English as a Foreign Language in Vietnam reasoned professionally about generative artificial intelligence. The study combined semi-structured interviews with 13 teachers from 13 universities and an analysis of 88 policy and governance documents comprising 10 national, 7 ministerial, and 71 institutional documents. A documented search, screening, inventory, and staged coding procedure enabled the systematic identification, classification, and analysis of the document corpus. Interview and documentary data were analysed separately, first within cases and governance levels and then across cases using matrices and joint displays. Findings showed that teachers' professional reasoning was developed through continual negotiation between classroom realities and multi-level AI governance. Participants moved beyond their traditional roles as language experts to become learning designers, pedagogical facilitators, critical mentors, and ethical guides. They set context-appropriate boundaries for AI use, reframed ethics in terms of transparency and cognitive engagement, and adapted assessment to preserve evidence of student learning. The documents revealed a layered but uneven governance landscape. National strategies articulated broad directions; ministerial documents provided partial guidance; and institutional policies varied considerably. The integration of the two datasets showed that AI literacy, governance, assessment, ethics, and teacher agency were interconnected with teachers’ professional reasoning. The study proposed the governance-informed Identity-Agency-Ethics-Assessment Practices heuristic for understanding AI-mediated teacher professionalism.
topics: Ethics and Social Impacts of AI

documents.abstract: This systematic review, in the context of the Concerns-Based Adoption Model (CBAM) as the theoretical framework, reviewed science teachers' concerns about the implementation of Generative Artificial Intelligence (GenAI) tools in science education. The study aimed to investigate the stages of concern science teachers show, analyze the factors that cause concerns and assess the strategies that aid in facilitating the adoption of GenAI in science teaching. A Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic Reviews and Meta-Analyses (PRISMA) framework was used to structure the review, and a narrative thematic synthesis was applied to categorize and synthesize the results from the different studies. Literature was identified through Google Scholar by systematically developed search terms that included combinations of the concepts of GenAI tools and teacher concern constructs, the full Boolean search strategy is reported in the Methods section for the purposes of replicability. A total of 432 records were identified and then screened for eligibility and then peer-reviewed empirical studies published from 2022 to 2026 were included. The findings show that the majority of secondary science teachers are at the early CBAM stages, suggesting that the majority of teachers are still preoccupied with understanding and managing GenAI rather than understanding how it can influence student learning. It was found that concern level and intention to adopt work via different psychological mechanisms: adoptive intentions can be stronger than positive beliefs at high concern stages. This gap indicates the need for theory-based empirical studies on GenAI adoption in secondary science education. This review drew from a single database and did not include a formal quality appraisal, its conclusions should be read as an initial, theory-building synthesis rather than a fully instrument-validated account. These boundaries are made explicit in the methods sections.
topics: Artificial Intelligence in Healthcare and Education

documents.abstract: Digitalization has made technology-supported materials essential, yet their practical use remains inefficient. This study investigates the link between teachers’ technopedagogical competencies and their perspectives on integrating artificial intelligence (AI) into education. Using an explanatory sequential mixed-methods approach, research was conducted with 297 teachers in Gaziantep during the 2024–2025 academic year. Quantitative data was collected via an Intelligent TPACK framework scale, while qualitative insights were gathered through semi-structured interviews with 10 participants. Data analysis included t-tests, ANOVA, Scheffé post hoc tests, and content analysis. Results indicate that teachers' AI-related technopedagogical skills are at a low-to-moderate level. While gender showed no significant difference, variables such as age, seniority and prior experience with Web 2.0 or AI tools caused notable differences. Qualitatively, teachers reported using AI for instructional design, assessment efficiency, and professional development. However, concerns were raised regarding data security, overreliance, and the lack of emotional depth in AI interactions. Ultimately, the study concludes that AI should serve as a complementary tool rather than a replacement for teachers.

Artificial intelligence (AI) is increasingly integrated into healthcare systems globally, including diagnostics, predictive analytics, and public health surveillance. AI adoption is increasing, yet fragile and resource-limited settings face distinct ethical and legal challenges. Lebanon provides a complex case: since 2019, the country has experienced economic collapse, workforce migration, rising non-communicable diseases, and sustained refugee influx, alongside rapid digital expansion. In 2026, the Ministry of Public Health launched the National Digital Health Transformation Strategy (2025–2030), recognizing AI as a potential lever to strengthen services and rebuild public trust. However, national ethical and legal standards specific to healthcare AI remain underdeveloped. In this perspective report, we present AI opportunities, legal gaps, and ethical risks within Lebanon’s fragmented public–private system. AI offers potential benefits in clinical decision support, public health surveillance, workforce support, and medical education. Yet algorithmic bias, data protection weaknesses, regulatory ambiguity, and unclear liability expose patients and professionals to uncertainty. Lebanon currently operates within a regulatory gray zone, as existing healthcare system and data laws predate machine-learning-based decision systems. Drawing on international ethical frameworks and pluralistic moral traditions, we propose an ethical containment strategy grounded in human dignity, accountability, transparency, and equity. We outline ten pillars, including human-led decision-making, sector-specific governance within the Ministry of Public Health (MOPH), bias containment, strengthened data protection and cybersecurity, clarified legal responsibility, professional training, participatory oversight, and lifecycle evaluation. Ethical containment does not resist innovation; rather, it seeks to ensure that AI strengthens resilience and trust instead of amplifying systematic vulnerabilities. The credibility and acceptance of AI in Lebanon will depend more on the strength of its ethical and institutional frameworks than on the sophistication of the technology itself.

documents.abstract: Everyone seems to be thinking about so-called artificial intelligence (AI) these days. As scientists, we understand that we're not about to have a conscious computer intelligence taking over the world, but we're nevertheless concerned about how "large language models" (LLMs) and AI "agents" are impacting the way that we do science. This concern has generated several recent essays about the effects of AI on research, including in my own field of astronomy and astrophysics. These opinion pieces tend to miss the biggest current concern for those whose jobs combine teaching with research - although the threat to future scientific research as we know it is probably a bit concerning, the effect on teaching is an existential crisis right now! We need to hang on to the parts of education that we think are at its core - so that students coming out of degree programmes are actually able to think for themselves, "like an astrophysicist". This means emphasising to students that they should use AI tools to support their education and not to replace it. One way of explaining the importance of this principle is to point out that students should be training their own neural networks.

Artificial intelligence can deliver substantial task-level efficiency gains without generating equivalent organizational value. This Research Note conceptualizes this disconnect as the AI efficiency trap and introduces conversion loss as the mechanism through which local gains dissipate across organizational value flows. Four forms of conversion loss are identified: coordination, continuity, verification, and governance loss. Building on research on IT business value, digital transformation, AI capability, omnichannel integration, and human–AI collaboration, the paper develops a value-conversion framework. It argues that organizational complementarity, task-appropriate omnichannel integration, human–AI task fit, and end-to-end outcome feedback determine whether AI-enabled efficiencies survive their transmission into customer, business, and risk outcomes. The framework shifts attention from AI adoption toward the organizational conditions required for value realization at scale.

Abstract Artificial Intelligence has rapidly become part of everyday communication, writing, education, media, and digital culture. While language has been traditionally understood as a human-created and his lexicon continuously evolving system, the emergence of generative AI raises a new question: Can machines become participants in language change? This paper examines the relationship between Artificial Intelligence and the formation of new words, expressions, and meanings. It focuses particularly on neologisms and word-formation processes, including Conversion, blending, compounding, clipping, acronym, affixation, and reduplication. The study argues that AI may not independently “own” or control language change, but it can increasingly act as a catalyst, amplifier, and collaborator in the evolution of vocabulary.

The recent success of gene drive mosquitoes suppressing malaria signals a new era in vector control. Yet, reliance on secreted, natural peptides poses risks of instability, host toxicity and resistance evolution. We propose synthesizing two transformative technologies to overcome these limits: generative AI for de novo peptide design and precision membrane tethering. Proof-of-concept work shows tethering antimicrobial peptides to the gut epithelium boosts potency 100-fold. Converging these approaches enables engineering of 'smart' immune barriers-AI-designed peptides optimized for stability and specificity, anchored to create impassable surfaces for pathogens. This 't-AMP' platform potentially offers a durable, fitter and broadly applicable strategy, extending rational vector engineering from mosquitoes to ticks and sandflies, revolutionizing control of multiple neglected diseases.

The dichotomy between religious knowledge and science in the madrasah education system in Indonesia has created an epistemological gap that hinders the development of students' scientific literacy and erodes the depth of their religious beliefs. This study aims to analyze the effectiveness of the Biology-Fiqh integrative approach in improving scientific literacy and religious beliefs of students at Madrasah Aliyah Muhammadiyah in Bima City. This study adopted a quasi-experimental design with a pre-test-post-test control group design involving 68 eleventh-grade students divided into an experimental group (n=34) and a control group (n=34). The research instruments included an adapted PISA 2022 framework-based scientific literacy test, a validated religious belief scale, a cognitive engagement observation sheet, and a semi-structured interview guide. Data analysis used ANCOVA, Cohen's d effect size test, and thematic analysis for qualitative data. The results showed that the experimental group experienced a significant increase in scientific literacy (M gain = 28.4; d = 1.12; p < 0.001) compared to the control group (M gain = 11.7; d = 0.48). Religious belief also increased significantly in the experimental group (M gain = 19.6; d = 0.89; p < 0.001). Qualitative analysis revealed four main themes: transformation of epistemological perspectives, strengthening of Muslim-scientist identity, resolution of cognitive conflict between science and religion, and learning motivation based on religious meaning-making. This study contributes to the development of a contextual integrative pedagogical model for madrasahs in eastern Indonesia and offers an operational framework for teachers in implementing science integration based on Islamic values.

A substantial body of previous research has examined gamification in educational settings, particularly its associations with self-determination, cognitive engagement, and critical thinking skills. However, there remain limitations in the analysis of gamification in relation to these constructs within vocational education. Therefore, this study was conducted to investigate the relationships among self-determination, cognitive engagement, and critical thinking skills in a learning process that incorporates gamification elements. A total of 309 students participated in this research and provided the data. The analysis was carried out using SmartPLS 3, applying Structural Equation Modelling (SEM) and Importance–Performance Map Analysis (IPMA). Based on the analytical results, there is a positive and significant relationship between self-determination and cognitive engagement. Furthermore, self-determination and cognitive engagement were positively associated with critical thinking skills. However, this study has limitations that should be acknowledged, as the data were obtained through self-report measures, which are subject to subjectivity and potential response bias. Therefore, future research is recommended to strengthen methodological rigor, both in terms of data collection and research approach, such as through qualitative studies and mixed-method designs.

ABSTRACTArtificial intelligence is progressing from passive analysis of scientific data toward activeparticipation in scientific experimentation. AI systems can increasingly analyze observations,propose experimental configurations, select subsequent actions, operate laboratory equipment,modify experimental strategies, and evaluate resulting data. This paper introduces the concept of the Autonomous AI Observer (AAIO): an artificialintelligence capable of independently selecting among physically permitted conditions, timing,bases, or configurations of a quantum measurement and subsequently initiating, observing,recording, analyzing, and responding to the resulting physical measurement. documents.abstract: The transition from traditional Personnel Administration to Strategic Human Capital Management (HCM) redefines human assets from operational costs to the primary source of sustainable competitive advantage. However, executing this strategic vision in a post-pandemic environment presents unprecedented challenges. This theoretical paper systematically reflects upon the literature mapping the evolution of HCM. It applies the Resource-Based View (RBV) and the VRIO framework to analyze the synergistic impact of modern trends: Employee Experience (EX), organizational agility, continuous learning, and inclusion. The conceptual synthesis reveals that implementing these modern HCM imperatives creates a systemic "complexity gap." Organizations face a limitation of scalability, where the cognitive and analytical capacities of traditional management are overwhelmed by the need for hyper-personalization and massive data volumes. Artificial Intelligence (AI) is identified as a theoretical necessity rather than a mere technological upgrade. AI systems provide the augmented intelligence required to bridge the complexity gap. However, the paper critically highlights that this integration must navigate significant ethical risks, including algorithmic bias and privacy concerns, to ensure sustainable human-AI symbiosis.

documents.abstract: The development of advanced artificial intelligence is increasingly concentrated in a small group of vertically integrated technology companies. These firms control combinations of computing infrastructure, cloud services, data, foundation models, software ecosystems, and channels of distribution. This article argues that such concentration transforms market power into a form of private governance over the conditions in which fundamental rights are exercised. Drawing on an interdisciplinary narrative review, it examines how concentration affects equality of access, privacy, freedom of science, working conditions, access to essential resources, environmental protection, and the availability of effective remedies. Evidence from data-centre expansion in Ireland, the United Kingdom, the United States, and Chile, together with studies of automation and collective bargaining, shows that benefits may be widely distributed while decision-making power and economic returns remain concentrated. Concentration does not itself establish a rights violation, but it increases dependency, opacity, switching costs, and the risk that social and environmental costs are externalised. The article concludes that competition policy must be combined with rights-based impact assessment, interoperability, public research capacity, worker participation, and enforceable access to review and remedy.
topics: Ethics and Social Impacts of AI

documents.abstract: Although employees often have limited control over task assignments, schedules, or collaboration partners, they may still have discretion in how they carry out tasks. Building on Job Demands-Resources theory, we integrate information-processing perspectives of play to propose that playful work design – proactively adding elements of fun and competition to routine activities – can be useful even in tightly structured jobs by increasing activated positive affect and reducing exhaustion. We tested this proposition in a 20-day diary study among 57 Norwegian naval cadets, yielding 1,046 day-level observations, using multilevel structural equation modeling. On days when cadets designed their work playfully, they reported more activated positive affect and less exhaustion. Combining designing fun with designing competition amplified these benefits. Thus, small discretionary choices in how employees approach work may produce immediate well-being gains in low-discretion roles and offer a micro-level pathway through which play at work can support performance.

Self-attention gives LLMs fine-grained, query-dependent access to context, but dense token interactions incur quadratic prefill cost and a key--value cache growing with context length. Research thus spans explicit-memory compression, sparse access, recurrent state construction, structured state dynamics, and heterogeneous mechanism composition. This survey analyzes these developments as model-internal contextual memory. We introduce a five-dimensional lens---Memory Representation, Memory Update, Access, Readout, and Integration---describing what is represented, how it changes, what is query-eligible, how it is read, and how readouts form outputs. This lens compares overlapping research lines without imposing one computational model. We reconstruct mechanism-level developments and architectural adoption using 59 release-level records from 14 major model lineages and 11 high-performing open-weight endpoints. First, explicit-memory and recurrent-state methods retain distinct interfaces but increasingly control overlapping memory functions. Second, heterogeneous architectures increasingly coordinate across network depth: layer-wise composition distributes complementary memory processing across representational stages, while cross-layer reuse carries selected memory and routing artifacts forward. Depth thus becomes a dimension along which contextual memory is constructed and managed. Third, these developments motivate a stateful multidimensional memory-routing hypothesis: persistent memory is organized across temporal scope, network depth, substrate type, and representation granularity, while coordinated Sparse Write and Sparse Read determine what is maintained and what contributes to each query. Overall, efficient sequence architecture design increasingly concerns the organization, lifecycle, and selective use of contextual memory rather than an isolated Attention operator.

Abstract Code completion entails the task of providing missing tokens given a surrounding context. It can boost developer productivity and serve as a code discovery tool. Code completion has recently been approached with Large Language Models (LLMs) fine-tuned on code (code LLMs). The performance of code LLMs can be assessed with downstream and intrinsic metrics. Downstream metrics are usually employed to evaluate the practical utility of a model, but can be unreliable and require complex calculations and domain-specific knowledge. In contrast, intrinsic metrics such as perplexity, entropy, and mutual information, which measure model confidence or uncertainty, are simple, versatile, and universal across LLMs and tasks, and have been proposed as proxies for functional correctness and hallucination risk in LLM-generated code. Motivated by this, we evaluate the confidence of LLMs when generating code by measuring code perplexity across programming languages, models, and datasets using various LLMs, and a sample of 2254 files from 881 GitHub projects. We find that strongly-typed languages exhibit lower perplexity than dynamically typed languages. Scripting languages also demonstrate higher perplexity. Shell appears universally high in perplexity, whereas Java appears low. Code perplexity depends on the employed LLM; under a fixed model, relative language-level rankings are largely stable across evaluation corpora. Although code comments modestly increase perplexity, the language ranking based on perplexity is barely affected by their presence. LLM researchers, developers, and users can use our findings to assess the suitability of LLM-based code completion in specific software projects based on how language, model choice, and code characteristics impact model confidence.

This article focuses on the core judicial role of giving reasons for a judge’s decision and the use of generative artificial intelligence (‘GenAI’) tools based on LLMs in the crafting of judgments. Considering specifically GenAI and judgment writing in common law systems, it deals with the connection between the act of decision-making and the giving of reasons for that decision. Our argument is that judgment writing should remain the domain of human judges, for reasons that are both institutional (the impact on the judicial system) and individual or processual (the impact on judges performing their roles). We seek to analyse the nature and extent of judicial use of GenAI tools that preserves this as a human domain. Ultimately, we conclude that it is not appropriate to use GenAI for judgment writing, but peripheral or adjacent uses may be supportable, provided they do not undercut the core judicial role.
topics: Ethics and Social Impacts of AI

documents.abstract: The rapid advancement of generative artificial intelligence has enabled the creation of highly realistic synthetic images, raising concerns regarding the authenticity of digital media. While convolutional neural network (CNN)-based methods have shown promising results for synthetic image detection, deep architectures often suffer from training instability caused by the vanishing gradient problem and limited representation learning. This study proposes a Deep Residual BiLSTM Fusion model that integrates residual-based CNN feature extraction with bidirectional long short-term memory (BiLSTM) modeling to enhance training stability and contextual representation learning. The proposed model is evaluated on the CIFAKE dataset, a challenging low-resolution benchmark for synthetic image detection. Experimental results demonstrate competitive performance with an accuracy of 97.27% and balanced precision and recall across both real and synthetic classes. Gradient flow analysis further confirms stable optimization behavior, highlighting the effectiveness of the proposed hybrid architecture for robust synthetic image detection.
topics: Generative Adversarial Networks and Image Synthesis

documents.abstract: Abstract In recent times, artificial intelligence (AI) is emerging as a revolutionary transformative force in various sectors of the contemporary society. It has rapidly becomes an integral part of our daily lives. Now a days AI plays crucial role in transforming various aspects of society and generate new possibilities and opportunities. The paper also present a dissection of an impact of AI on different aspects of the society including agriculture, industry, education, market, finance, business, transportation, employment, healthcare etc. This article is presented in a narrative review. The main object of this research paper is an attempt to find and to analyze the positive and negative impact of artificial intelligence on various field of the society. This research paper provides a comprehensive overview of the impact of AI on various aspects of the society in the form of dynamic nature of economy, transformation in education system, modern and advanced healthcare system, change in nature of employment and ethics etc. The collected literature for this research paper is focused on socio-economic influence as well as future fear and challenges in implementing of AI. The AI related literature shows that it has large potential to provide significant benefits for the present modern society but it has also aware us about challenges and risk in implementing of AI technology. Because of many scientists, technologists and others concerned with the welfare of society have started fearing about the extensive use of AI and its impacts on the society. The medical field is more affected by use of AI technology. It plays a crucial role in diagnosis, surgery, appropriate treatment methods and other related healthcare services. It can also play an important role in education transforming with student personalized learning experience for student and teacher also. However, we cannot ignore some problems about using of AI in the field of viability of employment, economic inequality, and ethical issues. In short, this research paper provides a comprehensive overview of the impact of AI on various aspects of the present society life.

documents.abstract: With the rapid development of mobile technology, mobile-assisted language learning has become increasingly prevalent in foreign language education. Duolingo is one of the most popular language learning applications. However, there is still limited evidence about its effectiveness in improving Chinese vocabulary learning, especially among primary school students. The purpose of this study is to examine the effects of Duolingo-assisted learning on Chinese vocabulary acquisition among primary school students and to examine students’ motivation toward Chinese vocabulary learning. A quantitative quasi-experimental design was adopted. Fifty primary school students participated in the study. A Chinese vocabulary pre-test and post-test were administered to measure learning achievement, while a learning motivation questionnaire was used to examine students’ motivation toward Chinese vocabulary learning. The results of a one-way ANCOVA revealed that students in the experimental group achieved significantly higher post-test vocabulary scores than those in the control group after controlling for pre-test scores. Furthermore, the results of a one-way MANOVA indicated that the experimental group demonstrated significantly higher self-efficacy motivation, whereas no statistically significant differences were found in intrinsic motivation, self-determination, or grade motivation. These findings suggest that Duolingo-assisted learning can effectively enhance Chinese vocabulary achievement and strengthen students’ confidence in learning Chinese vocabulary. The study provides empirical evidence supporting the integration of mobile-assisted language learning applications into primary Chinese language instruction and offers practical implications for teachers and educators.

This research aims to examine organizational ergonomics and its impact on job burnout among a random sample of teaching and administrative staff employed at universities, colleges, and institutes within higher education institutions in Iraq. This topic is of considerable importance because improving organizational ergonomics can enhance the work environment, increase job performance, and promote employee well-being. The research also seeks to address the problem of occupational stress and excessive workloads resulting from increasing teaching and administrative tasks assigned to employees in higher education institutions. These pressures contribute to higher levels of job burnout and adversely affect employee performance and job satisfaction. A descriptive-analytical approach was adopted, and data were collected using a structured questionnaire administered to a random sample of teaching and administrative staff. A total of 108 valid questionnaires. The data were analyzed using the Statistical Package for the Social Sciences (SPSS) and the Analysis of Moment Structures (AMOS) program. The results showed a statistically significant positive correlation and influence between the two variables. This finding contradicts the prevailing theoretical trend in the literature. This result suggests the possibility of other organizational or psychological factors influencing this relationship within Iraqi higher education institutions. Accordingly, the study recommends that decision-makers in Iraqi higher education institutions should move beyond the mere implementation of ergonomic practices and adopt a comprehensive approach that integrates improvements to the physical work environment with psychological and social support, while proactively managing employee expectations to reduce job burnout and enhance organizational effectiveness.

LLM services are billed per token and context windows are measured in tokens, yet the number of tokens needed for the same content varies across languages. We measure this token premium on seven tokenizers of widely used 2026 models (OpenAI o200k, Llama 3, Qwen3, DeepSeek V3/V4, Gemma 3, Mistral Tekken, and the Claude generation-5 tokenizer via Anthropic's counting API) on NTREX-128 (124 non-English reference translations) and on the Universal Declaration of Human Rights for regional languages. French requires 31% to 58% more tokens than English, whereas Simplified Chinese ranges from 5% fewer to 40% more and is cheaper than French on six of the seven tokenizers. Regional and overseas languages of France pay roughly 1.6 to 3.3 times the English count. We discuss how history re-sending, tiered pricing and fixed context windows amplify the absolute gap in agentic use. In a controlled experiment (BPE, Europarl, 50k vocabulary), adding French to tokenizer training data quickly reduces the premium, with diminishing returns and a growing cost for English. Finally, we present Baracoda FR v1.2, a byte-level BPE prototype with Tekken's vocabulary size. On a final test of six corpora never consulted during design, with a protocol declared fixed beforehand, it uses 11.5% fewer tokens than Tekken on French and 3.7% fewer on English; results hold after removing test sentences overlapping the training data and with an equal ordinary-token budget. It is worse on other languages and, at comparable vocabulary size, does not outperform CroissantLLM. These are segmentation results only; effects on model quality and task cost remain to be shown.

Abstract India’s Viksit Bharat @2047 vision requires a knowledge-driven digital economy powered by artificial intelligence, inclusive entrepreneurship, FinTech, e-commerce and sustainable practices. Library and Information Science (LIS) institutions remain under-utilised as active intermediaries between knowledge resources and the competencies demanded by the future of work. This paper coins the Knowledge-Commerce Bridge (KCB) Framework—an original, multi-layered LIS model that positions academic and public libraries as AI-enabled hubs for digital-commerce literacy, ethical information services and sustainable innovation. The study adopts a conceptual-constructive design that synthesises LIS theory, digital-economy literature, AI-ethics guidelines and national policy documents (NEP-2020, Digital India, Startup India). The KCB Framework comprises four interdependent layers: (1) Infrastructure and Multilingual Access, (2) AI Knowledge Processing, (3) User-Centric Commerce Services and (4) Ethical-Sustainable Governance. Expected outcomes include reduced information asymmetry for gig workers and micro-entrepreneurs, strengthened academia–industry–startup linkages, and measurable contributions to inclusive growth and the Sustainable Development Goals. The framework is offered as a replicable, emulable blueprint that other institutions can adapt, pilot and scale, thereby leaving a durable mark on both scholarship and practice.
topics: Library Collection Development and Digital Resources

documents.abstract: Introduction: Robotic-assisted reverse shoulder arthroplasty is a new technology which could lead to more accurate implant positioning and potentially improved longevity and outcomes. Cognitive workload and learning curve must be considered when introducing new technologies into the operating theatre. Materials and methods: The first 20 patients who received a MAKO robotic shoulder arthroplasty performed by a single surgeon during limited release access to this technology were evaluated. The surgeon learning curve was assessed in the domains of operative time and via the NASA Task Load Index (NASA-TLX) score. Results: = .42, with poor correlation ρ = -0.198). The NASA-TLX score showed the learning curve breakpoint between three and five cases across the six domains and composite score. There was one intraoperative technical complication, where the robot had to be re-started midway through the operation. Discussion: The NASA-TLX score is a more reliable judge of learning curve than operative time for MAKO robotic-assisted shoulder arthroplasties, showing a learning curve breakpoint after three to five cases across different cognitive domains. Level of evidence: Level IV - prospective observational study.

This study explores the legal and ethical problems arising from the integration of artificial intelligence technologies into the administrative and public-service systems of Algeria. It asks how far the country's existing legislative arsenal and its rules of digital ethics can absorb the accelerating development of intelligent systems, and assesses the role of the existing digital infrastructure in securing that transition. The paper adopts a descriptive-analytical methodology: the descriptive component inventories the relevant legal instruments and the available technical capacity, while the analytical component performs a gap analysis of whether texts drafted for classical digitisation can accommodate concepts such as the legal personality of a robot or liability for an algorithmic act, and subjects current digital administrative practice to critique against international ethical standards of transparency, fairness and non-discrimination. The study concludes that there is a clear legislative gap in the attribution of legal responsibility for algorithmic acts, particularly under the personal data protection legislation, because Algerian civil and criminal liability alike presuppose a discerning, willing human author whom an autonomous and opaque system does not supply. It further finds that the digital infrastructure, and specifically data centres and the national cloud, is the cornerstone of digital sovereignty and of ethical privacy, provided it is reinforced by an advanced cybersecurity framework and by reduced dependence on closed foreign platforms. The study recommends the drafting of a dedicated national legal framework and ethical charter for artificial intelligence, balancing technological innovation against the protection of the fundamental rights of the Algerian citizen.

documents.abstract: As artificial Intelligence (AI) is having an increasing influence on the consumer-brand relationship, empirical evidence of the effects of AI-powered real-time communication on emotional brand engagement over time is scarce. Based on the Digital Emotional Brand Engagement (DEBE) model consisting of four outcome dimensions (Affective Engagement, Cognitive Engagement, Behavioral Engagement, Identification, and Emotional Attachment). The study proposes and empirically tests a model of four dimensions of AI interactions (Responsiveness and Availability, Personalization, Conversational Quality, Problem Resolution Efficiency). A descriptive-correlational quantitative design was adopted, and a sample of 400 consumers who had recently used AI-powered customer service was drawn. Multiple regression analysis and structural equation modeling (SEM) were used for analysis of the data, as well as mediation and moderation analysis (PROCESS macro). By considering all four dimensions of the interaction between people and artificial intelligence together, we could explain 52.1% of the variance in DEBE. The beta value for Affective Engagement was the largest for Responsiveness and Availability, while the highest beta value for Identification and Emotional Attachment was for Personalization. The overall path coefficient of the complete model from AI interaction to DEBE was 0.714. Partial mediation was observed between the quality of AI interaction and behavioral engagement with Identification and Emotional Attachment, and Digital Literacy had a significant moderating effect on the relationship between the quality of AI interaction and the emotional engagement of the consumer. The results highlight how critical an AI-powered customer service can be for boosting customers' emotional connection with brands in an e-marketing environment.

Artificial intelligence changes what organizations can do; human leadership must decide what should be done, what remains accountable, and what must never be surrendered to machines. This working paper presents FILE: The Five Intelligences of Leadership Evolution as a human-centered management theory and diagnostic framework for responsible leadership and decision-making in the age of artificial intelligence and robotics. FILE argues that the most important human skills for the AI era and the future of work require the integrated exercise of five meta-intelligences: Augmented Intelligence, Emotional Intelligence, Cultural Intelligence, Political Intelligence, and Adaptive Intelligence. The paper defines the FILE formula, maps the framework onto the human hand, presents the 70 foundational nested intelligences, the 128-intelligence Teaching and Diagnostic Framework, and the 163-intelligence Extended Taxonomy, explains five emergent outcomes, and develops RC: The Relational Commons as the shared human ecosystem that leadership must protect, cultivate, and renew. It also clarifies boundaries among adjacent intelligences, offers a diagnostic application to AI-supported employee performance evaluation, and states limitations and future research directions. Its purpose is to establish a public, citable, and timestamped record of FILE as a transdisciplinary theory of human leadership in the age of AI and robots.

The article is devoted to the study of the admissibility and limits of the use of artificial intelligence in the system of state management of land resources of the Republic of Kazakhstan. The main directions of implementing artificial intelligence technologies in cadastral and land management processes are examined, including the automation of geospatial data processing, forecasting changes in land use, and the integration of analytical results into managerial decision-making processes. Special attention is paid to the legal regulation of the use of artificial intelligence in land resource management based on the Law of the Republic of Kazakhstan dated November 17, 2025, No. 230-VIII “On Artificial Intelligence”. The application of specialized scripts containing elements of artificial intelligence for the automation of cadastral and land management activities is analyzed. Examples of the use of modern geographic information systems based on machine learning algorithms in spatial analysis and land monitoring tasks are presented. The article demonstrates the practical possibilities of applying artificial intelligence for calculating vegetation indices, automated monitoring of land resource conditions, and detecting violations in land use. The key advantages of AI implementation are identified, including improved data accuracy, reduced influence of the human factor, and optimization of time and material resources. The main problems and limitations associated with the digitalization of land relations are determined, including the need for data standardization, adaptation of the regulatory framework, and the development of methodological foundations for the application of artificial intelligence in the public law sphere.

The aim of this study is to examine the relationship between artificial intelligence anxiety and career decidedness among athletes and to determine whether these variables differ according to certain demographic characteristics. The research was conducted with a sample of 392 athletes competing in different sports disciplines. The sample consisted of 122 female and 270 male athletes, with a mean age of 20.67 years. Data were collected using validated and reliable measurement tools, including the Artificial Intelligence Anxiety Scale (AIAS) and the Career Decidedness Scale (CDS). After confirming that the assumptions required for parametric analyses were met, descriptive statistics, independent samples t-tests, MANOVA, ANOVA, and correlation analyses were employed. The MANOVA results indicated a statistically significant difference only in the “artificial intelligence configuration” sub-dimension of the AIAS based on gender, with female athletes scoring higher than male athletes. Correlation analyses showed a low-level, negative, and statistically significant relationship between the “learning” sub-dimension of the AIAS and CDS scores (p < 0.05). Conversely, a low-level, positive, and statistically significant relationship was found between the “sociotechnical blindness” sub-dimension of the AIAS and CDS scores (p < 0.05). These findings suggest that athletes who experience higher levels of anxiety related to learning processes involving artificial intelligence tend to exhibit greater career indecision, whereas athletes who are less sensitive to the potential risks and threats associated with artificial intelligence technologies demonstrate greater decisiveness in their career choices. Future research may further expand on these findings by investigating the impact of awareness and education programs on athletes’ career decision-making processes.

documents.abstract: There are two primary ways to boost profits: increase revenues or decrease expenses. For example, whether a company increases revenues by $1 million or decreases expenses by $1 million, its profits will increase by $1 million (all else equal). But how do people subjectively evaluate such changes to revenues and expenses, and what inferences do they draw as a result? Across nine experiments ( N = 6045), an archival data analysis, and four supplemental studies, we document a robust “revenue halo” effect: increases in revenues, relative to equivalent decreases in expenses, lead to more positive perceptions of profitability, in both the short and long run, and result in more favorable overall impressions of financial strength, performance, potential, and trajectory. Consequently, managers who propose ideas for increasing revenues (vs. decreasing expenses) are viewed as more competent; consultants who develop such strategies are more likely to be rehired; and companies that report higher revenues are more attractive to investors. We furthermore propose that the revenue halo effect can be explained, in part, by the belief that strategies for increasing revenues are more innovative than strategies for decreasing expenses. Finally, to underscore the real-world relevance of our account, we analyze approximately 13 million financial news articles, finding that when firms reported increased revenues (vs. decreased expenses), they subsequently rose in Fortune 's “World's Most Admired Companies” rankings (the following year). This research identifies a novel asymmetry in judgments of organizational performance, with implications for managerial decision-making, corporate communication, and capital allocation.

This article analyses the role of artificial intelligence (AI) technologies in developing the professional competence of English language teachers, their pedagogical potential, and the methodological conditions required for their effective use. In contemporary education, the development of AI technologies is transforming the content of teachers’ professional activities and bringing such areas as lesson design, educational material development, personalised learning, assessment, feedback provision, and pedagogical reflection to a new level. Systematic studies published in 2026 indicate that language teachers are using generative AI (GenAI) technologies for lesson planning, the development of educational materials, and the support of writing activities; at the same time, they reveal competency needs related to AI literacy, technical skills, ethical decision-making, and data privacy. The article also proposes a pedagogical model for developing English language teachers’ competence in working with AI technologies. Keywords: artificial intelligence, AI technologies, English language teacher, professional competence, AI literacy, digital competence, pedagogical competence

Purpose - This study examines the requirements for employing artificial intelligence (AI) in Qur'anic education and interpretation, focusing on how Qur'anic scholars and instructors in Fars Province, Iran, perceive the conditions necessary for its effective, ethical, and pedagogically appropriate use. Design/methodology/approach - The study adopts a qualitative phenomenological design using Colaizzi's seven-step analytical procedure. Data were collected through in-depth, semi-structured interviews with ten faculty members in Qur'anic sciences and Hadith and experienced Qur'anic instructors in Fars Province. Participants were selected through purposive and theoretical sampling until theoretical saturation was achieved. The interview data were subjected to thematic analysis, with credibility, dependability, confirmability, and transferability addressed through validation procedures. Findings - The analysis generated three principal categories: preliminary and infrastructural requirements, foundational and principled requirements, and technical and operational requirements. These comprised eight subcategories and 45 sub-concepts. The findings indicate that AI can support personalized learning, Qur'anic recitation, comprehension, multimodal instruction, and the integration of Qur'anic knowledge. However, its effective use requires reliable infrastructure, organized and credible Qur'anic data, trained educators, ethical safeguards, source verification, content validation, professional supervision, and interdisciplinary cooperation. Research implications/limitations - The framework provides practical guidance for educational institutions, Qur'anic centers, policymakers, and technology developers. However, the study is limited by its ten participants from a single province and its reliance on self-reported perceptions rather than observed AI-supported instruction. Originality/value - The study provides an empirically grounded phenomenological framework that connects AI, Qur'anic pedagogy, and ethical requirements for sacred-text education, extending AI-in-education research into the specific epistemic context of Qur'anic learning and interpretation.

documents.abstract: Objective — to systematize current data on the endotypes and biomarkers of chronic urticaria (CU) and to analyze the potential applications of artificial intelligence (AI) in patient phenotyping, particularly in predicting response to antihistamines (AH) and other treatment modalities. Materials and methods. A literature search was conducted in the PubMed/MEDLINE, Scopus, and Web of Science databases for the period 2018—2025 using the key terms: «chronic urticaria», «biomarkers», «endotype», «artificial intelligence», «machine learning», «omalizumab», «antihistamines», and «treatment response». Forty-five sources meeting the inclusion criteria were selected. Results and discussions. The endotype concept of chronic spontaneous urticaria (CSU) — type I (autoallergic) and type IIb (autoimmune) — is key to understanding the clinical heterogeneity of the disease and provides the theoretical basis for biomarker profiling. Leading biomarkers include total IgE, IgG anti-FcεRI, IgG anti-TPO, the functional ASST and BAT assays, C-reactive protein, D-dimer, and basophil and eosinophil counts. Among AI-based tools, the most clinically validated is the prognostic calculator developed by J. Sánchez et al. (2024—2025), which predicts response to antihistamines with an accuracy of 78.6 % (AUC 0.829) based on 6 clinical variables, without requiring any laboratory tests. Conclusions. The combination of biomarker profiling and AI technologies offers a genuine path toward personalized management of patients with CU. Priorities include standardizing biomarker threshold values, external validation of predictive models, and establishing a regulatory framework for implementing AI in clinical practice.

Background: Job alienation is an important organizational issue that may negatively affect employees’ attachment to their work. However, the actual level of job alienation and its relationship with conscious leadership remain unclear, creating a practical need for investigation. Objectives: This study aims to examine the relationship between conscious leadership and job alienation among employees at the Presidency of Sulaymaniyah Municipality, assess the statistical relationship between conscious leadership and job alienation, and determine which dimensions make significant predictive contributions to job alienation. Methods: The study adopted a descriptive-analytical approach. The study population comprised approximately 520 employees, and 250 questionnaires were distributed, 233 were returned, and 220 valid questionnaires were retained for analysis. Data were collected using a five-point Likert-scale questionnaire and analyzed using SPSS version 25 through descriptive statistics, Cronbach’s alpha, Pearson’s correlation, and simple and multiple linear regression. Results: The findings showed that conscious leadership was perceived at a relatively high level, with Cognitive Awareness representing the most prominent dimension. Job alienation was at a relatively low to moderate level, with Normlessness being the most prominent dimension and Social Isolation the least prominent. A statistically significant negative relationship was found between conscious leadership and job alienation, and conscious leadership made a statistically significant negative contribution to the prediction of job alienation. At the dimensional level, Self-Awareness and Cognitive Awareness made statistically significant negative unique contributions, whereas Awareness of Others and Situational Awareness did not demonstrate statistically significant unique contributions. Conclusion: The findings indicate a statistically significant negative association between conscious leadership and job alienation. In particular, Self-Awareness and Cognitive Awareness made significant predictive contributions within the model, while the overall explanatory capacity remained limited, suggesting that other factors may also contribute to employees’ experiences of job alienation.

This article analyzes the role of modern state environmental policy in developing environmental culture and a responsible worldview among youth. The article substantiates that the human factor, particularly the transformation of the environmental consciousness of youth as the most dynamic segment of society, is of strategic importance in achieving environmental sustainability. The author examines the impact of legal, educational, and institutional reforms implemented by the state on the behavior and value system of young people.

This paper examines how row-wise renormalization affects Muon, focusing on the gap between NorMuon's worst-case guarantees and its practical performance (Li et al.). Despite its growing adoption and promising performance in large language model (LLM) pretraining, NorMuon's worst-case guarantees remain poorly understood. One fundamental question is: Does row normalization yield provable convergence gains, potentially through its interaction with approximate polar computation and exponential moving-average momentum? Our results show that row normalization introduces a dimension-dependent factor in the worst-case iteration complexity under the operator-norm geometry, which persists even with exact polar computation and any fixed momentum parameters. Indeed, we establish an algorithm-dependent lower bound and a matching upper bound in deterministic settings, and extend our upper bound analysis to stochastic settings. Both upper-bound analyses allow approximate polar computation. Experiments show that NorMuon is slower than Muon on synthetic problems inspired by our worst-case construction, yet outperforms Muon in LLM pretraining. These findings sharpen the puzzle of why row normalization helps in practice and complement the recent findings of Dewulf et al.

The construction sector is characterized by high organizational complexity derived from its temporary, dynamic, and process-specific nature. This industry registers some of the highest occupational accident rates worldwide. Within the European regulatory framework, Directive 92/57/EEC establishes the Health and Safety Plan (H&SP) as the principal instrument for preventive management on-site. In Spain, the transposition of this Directive introduced a preliminary design-phase document (Health and Safety Study or Basic Study, H&SS/H&SBS), intended to identify risks and define preventive measures that subsequently inform the contractor’s H&SP. Despite the importance of H&SS/H&SBS documents within the safety management process, empirical evidence remains limited regarding both their technical quality and their predictive capacity to explain the quality of subsequent H&SPs. This study addresses this gap through a qualitative and quantitative approach aimed at evaluating the intrinsic quality of H&SS/H&SBS and H&SP documents and modelling the dependency relationship between them. A database comprising 560 documents (280 H&SS/H&SBS and 280 H&SP) from 280 construction projects was assessed using a Delphi-based expert evaluation tool combined with a ratio weighting method. The results reveal consistently low levels of document quality and a limited capacity of H&SS/H&SBS to predict the quality of the corresponding H&SP. These findings suggest a systemic “cascade” failure in preventive planning, whereby documents frequently operate as instruments of formal compliance rather than as effective safety management tools. Our models’ findings support the need for effective audits and advanced technical training for professionals drafting these documents to improve preventive planning.

documents.abstract: Generative Artificial Intelligence (GenAI) is increasingly used by university students not only to locate information, but also to explain concepts, organize ideas, and complete academic tasks. This article examines the psychological processes that may explain why such use can support learning in some situations while reducing students' intellectual involvement in others. A conceptual literature review was conducted by bringing together foundational work on Distributed Cognition, Extended Mind, Cognitive Load, Student Engagement, and the ICAP Framework with recent studies on GenAI in education. Sources were selected for their relevance to cognitive offloading, cognitive engagement, and academic integrity. The review suggests that the educational consequences of GenAI depend less on its mere use than on how cognitive work is divided between students and the system. Offloading routine demands may free resources for evaluation and reflection, whereas delegating core reasoning may weaken engagement and make academic products less representative of students' own understanding. On this basis, the Educational Cognitive Transformation Model (ECTM) is proposed to connect learning transformation, cognitive offloading, redistribution of cognitive activities, cognitive engagement, learning quality, and academic integrity. ECTM is offered as a conceptual proposition that still requires empirical testing.

Abstract Background Trials methodology research priorities must be regularly reassessed to address contemporary methodological challenges. Over a decade has passed since the original priority setting exercise surveyed UK clinical trials unit directors. We conducted a two-stage international, multi-stakeholder survey to identify and rank current priorities in clinical trial methodology. Methods Stakeholders—researchers, trialists, healthcare professionals, patient and public representatives, funders, research ethics committee members, and others—were recruited through professional networks and snowball sampling. In stage 1, participants responded to four open-ended questions covering trial planning, conduct, analysis, and reporting. Responses were categorised into 34 research questions. In stage 2, participants reviewed the questions in random order, selected their top 10, and ranked them. Reverse scoring was applied, with scores summed within stakeholder groups, converted to rank-based scores, and combined so each group contributed equally regardless of size. Additional questions were independently coded by two authors against the 34 predefined questions, and new themes identified. Results In stage 1, 274 participants from 20 countries provided 2409 suggestions, categorised under 34 research questions. In stage 2, 431 respondents from 25 countries participated, of whom 341 (79%) across seven stakeholder groups completed priority ranking. The top 10 priority questions (including a joint seventh rank) were (1) designing relevant and impactful trials, (2) ensuring representative participants, (3) improving recruitment, (4) identifying and prioritising outcomes, (5) using healthcare systems data, (6) participant involvement in planning, (7=) transparency of trials, (7=) optimising trial approvals, (9) reporting and presenting findings, and (10) sharing and communicating findings. The top three questions appeared in all seven stakeholder groups’ top 10. Patient and public representatives ( n = 40) ranked ‘participant involvement in planning’ highest, while ethics committee members ( n = 9) uniquely prioritised ‘consent and safety’. ‘Innovative trials designs’ and ‘artificial intelligence in trials’ emerged as the most frequent new themes suggested. Conclusions This work provides an updated stakeholder-informed agenda for trials methodology research. The top three priorities were designing relevant and impactful trials, ensuring representative participants, and improving recruitment, each appeared in the top 10 for all stakeholder groups. Despite consensus on core priorities, differences between professional and patient-public stakeholders highlight areas for future methodology research and funding.

documents.abstract: BACKGROUND: Artificial Intelligence (AI) tools are increasingly used to improve efficiency, including in residency application review. While these technologies may streamline processes, their ability to identify optimal candidates for specific programs remains uncertain. This study aims to evaluate if AI can enhance the productivity of residency application review without compromising selection quality. METHODS: General surgery residency applications were analyzed using a large language model-based AI platform configured with customized program-specific weighting of applicant metrics. The AI-generated scores and rank list were compared with results from the traditional review process in which the application review committee manually reviews applications, scores applicants, and selects candidates for interview. RESULTS: A total of 847 applications were reviewed, and 96 applicants were manually selected (MS) for interviews by the application review committee. Of these, 32 (33%) were also ranked in the AI's top 96 candidates, including 7 in the top 10. Quartile analysis demonstrated that 51 (53.1%) MS candidates were in the top quartile of AI rankings, 26 (27.1%) in the second, 8 (8.3%) in the third, and 11 (11.4%) in the bottom. Adjusting the weights of various factors did not significantly alter these distributions. Technical review revealed scoring anomalies, including negligible AI scores for some candidates selected for interview. Analysis of the weighted factors showed that letters of recommendation contributed 29.4% of MS vs 25.1% of AI scoring (p = 0.009), research 6.3% vs 8.0% (p = 0.017), MSPE 7.4% vs 9.0% (p = 0.073), and factors such as USMLE and experiences were equivalent between the 2 groups. CONCLUSION: AI-assisted review may serve as a useful adjunct for initial screening but requires further refinement and training to better replicate human qualitative judgment. Future work will include evaluating concordance between AI rankings and the final program rank list and additional application review to guide software optimization and improve reliability as a screening tool.

documents.abstract: Ergonomics, as a scientific discipline, is gaining increasing importance in modern workplaces, as people spend more time engaged in work-related activities, often in static postures and under continuous technological exposure. Ergonomics focuses on adapting working conditions to match the physical and mental capabilities of humans, with the primary goals of enhancing productivity, ensuring safety, and improving overall employee well-being. Proper ergonomic practices help prevent workplace injuries, reduce fatigue, and create a healthier and more efficient work environment. One of the key roles of ergonomics is to reduce human fatigue during work processes. By designing tasks, tools, and workspaces that align with human capabilities, ergonomics minimizes unnecessary physical and mental strain. This not only improves worker comfort and health, but also contributes to clearer and more realistic standards for performing operations. As a result, ergonomics plays a vital role in increasing labor productivity and maintaining long-term efficiency in production environments. The emergence of new Industry 4.0 technologies such as automation, digitization, and artificial intelligence presents additional challenges for ergonomics. These rapid technological advancements require ongoing ergonomic adaptations to ensure safe, healthy, and sustainable work practices. This paper provides a comprehensive overview of the field of ergonomics and presents key ergonomic methods. Special attention is given to the software solution ErgoFellow 3.0, which includes various tools to assess and implement ergonomic improvements. The use of computer-aided ergonomics enables quick, accurate evaluations of working conditions, supporting a safer and more productive workplace.

Introduction: Occupational burnout among young adult professionals has reached concerning levels, and there are more people struggling with internet gaming disorder (IGD) each day. Studies suggest these two problems feed into each other. Burnout can drive people toward gaming as an escape, and gaming can reduce work performance, which in turn increases burnout. This literature review was conducted to discuss how occupational burnout, gaming addiction, and work performance relate to one another among young professionals. Methods: We searched the MEDLINE, PubMed, Scopus, and Web of Science databases from 2001 to 2025. Results: We included 52 relevant studies, and the findings show that each part of the cycle reinforces the others. Burnout increases escapism behaviors (r = 0.31-0.65), and escapism motivation is the strongest predictor of IGD among gaming motivations (r = 0.40); it also bridges the relationship between work stress and pathological gaming. Discuss: Most of the studies conclude that a vicious cycle exists where burnout could become gaming addiction through digital escapism, and gaming addiction decreases work productivity and then leads back into burnout. Digital escapism appears to be a crucial link in the chain. Addressing these problems requires intervention at multiple levels, organizational changes alongside individual support. Longitudinal research testing actual interventions would be a valuable next step. Conclusion: Growing interdependence between digital wellness and occupational health necessitates coordinated, multilevel interventions targeting individual, behavioral, organizational, and structural determinants. Given the substantial individual and economic burden, greater investment in longitudinal research, policy development, and rigorously evaluated interventions is essential.

The growing incidence of Non-Alcoholic Fatty Liver Disease (NAFLD) among night-shift IT professionals is posing as a major occupational health issue since shift work, sedentary lifestyle, psychosocial stress, lack of sleep, and disrupted circadian rhythms can lead to metabolism problems and fatty liver. Even though there is a possibility to cure NAFLD by adopting lifestyle changes, the pharmacological intervention for NAFLD is minimal and there is a high potential for the use of mind-body techniques like Rajayoga Meditation and Varma Therapy to enhance metabolic, psychological, and physiological well-being. The present study intended to determine the efficacy of Rajayoga Meditation and Varma Therapy on occupational stress and NAFLD among night-shift IT professionals. An interventional study was performed among 60 IT workers on night shift (aged between 25 and 45 years; 30 males and 30 females) suffering from NAFLD (Grades I and II), who participated in a protocol involving Rajayoga meditation and Varma therapy for a duration of 12 weeks. Parameters measured included Perceived Stress Scale (PSS-10), serum cortisol, lipid profile, levels of anxiety and depression, which were measured using the Depression Anxiety Stress Scale-21 (DASS-21), and status of liver, as determined by ultrasound scanning. Data analysis involved paired statistical test, with p<0.001 being regarded as statistically significant. Significant improvement was seen post-intervention in all the parameters mentioned above, including Perceived Stress Scale score, serum cortisol level, lipid profile levels, DASS-21 scores for anxiety and depression, and ultrasonography-based NAFLD grading. The results showed that Rajayoga meditation and Varma therapy could lead to significant improvements in psychological well-being, stress-related biomarkers, lipid metabolism, and NAFLD-related ultrasonographic features among night-shift IT professionals.
